title: The US Just Reversed Course on the Global Vaccine Alliance. India Had Already Pledged $20 Million.
excerpt: Rubio told Congress the State Department would re-engage with Gavi after a year-long funding freeze — a move driven by the Ebola outbreak and bipartisan pressure.
body:
In a significant policy reversal, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Congress on Tuesday that the State Department would re-engage with Gavi, the global vaccine alliance, after the Trump administration froze roughly $300 million in annual funding a year ago.

The announcement, made during Rubio's testimony before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, comes as a deadly Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda has killed hundreds and been declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern by the WHO.

## What Changed

The US pulled its funding from Gavi in June 2025 under the direction of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., a long-time vaccine skeptic who claimed the alliance had "ignored safety" — an assertion he provided no evidence to support.

The decision stripped Gavi of its single largest donor at a critical moment. The Geneva-based alliance, which helps the world's poorest countries purchase vaccines for children, had already fallen short of its $11.9 billion fundraising target for the 2026-2030 strategic cycle, securing only $9 billion in pledges.

Rubio said the reversal was driven by necessity. "We need to drive this to an outcome," he told lawmakers. He said Kennedy had taken a "leading role" in determining Gavi's future, but that the State Department had decided a few weeks ago to re-engage. "We'd like to get this issue resolved in an outcome that's acceptable both to Congress and also to our goals on global health."

## India's Quiet Commitment

While Washington wavered, India moved. At Gavi's replenishment conference last year, Indian Health Minister JP Nadda announced a $20 million contribution to the alliance's 2026-2030 cycle, citing India's role as a manufacturer of 60% of the world's vaccines.

"India pledges to support Gavi 6.0, echoing the vision of our Honourable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for fulfilling India's role as Vishwa Bandhu — a trusted partner to the world," Nadda said at the time.

India's Serum Institute of India remains the backbone of Gavi's supply chain, producing billions of doses of vaccines against diseases from measles to pneumonia at prices that make immunisation campaigns in sub-Saharan Africa financially viable.

## What Is at Stake

Gavi estimates that without full US funding, 75 million children could miss vaccinations and 1.2 million could die over the next five years. The Ebola outbreak has made the stakes impossible to ignore — the disease has spread across DRC and into Uganda, and Gavi has already committed $50 million to the response, including $40 million to accelerate vaccine development.

The re-engagement does not mean money is flowing yet. Rubio offered no timeline for restored funding, and the Trump administration's 2026 budget request excluded Gavi entirely. Congress, which approved $300 million for 2025, will ultimately decide the funding level.

## The Diaspora Dimension

For the 4.5 million Indian Americans in the US, the Gavi story sits at the intersection of two identities: their stake in American policy and their connection to India's global health leadership. Indian-origin researchers, physicians, and pharmaceutical executives are deeply embedded in the global vaccine ecosystem — from bench science at the NIH to manufacturing floors in Pune.

Rubio's reversal is a start. Whether it translates into restored funding will depend on Congress, Kennedy's continued influence, and the trajectory of an Ebola outbreak that has already forced the world's hand.
author: Diaspora Desk
